verdict.rationale: Better Auth is a self-hosted library that stores auth data in a database you configure (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and more), so data lives wherever you run that database. Community users confirm they own all the data and are not tied to any DB provider. However, nothing in the evidence explicitly addresses region selection or data residency. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of region or residency controls, compliance guidance on residency, any hosted-offering region options, and independent corroboration specific to residency.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Better Auth requires a database to store user data. You can easily configure Better Auth to use SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL, and more!
You get all of your auth data in your own db in 1 cli command. You are not tied to any db provider.
It just works and I own all the data.
